tool.name: LoCoHAdaptive
tool.summary: Adaptive (a-) Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) home-range and utilization-distribution estimator (Getz et al. 2007).
tool.usage:
Choosing a: the maximum cumulative length a controls how far the cumulative neighbour distance may extend before a local hull is closed. Larger a gives larger, smoother hulls; smaller a gives tighter, more fragmented hulls (too small, and many focal points have fewer than 3 neighbours and are skipped).
Getz et al. (2007) suggest, as a starting heuristic, a equal to the maximum distance between any pair of points (the default option here), then refining downward toward the value that minimizes the combined Type I and Type II error via the "minimum spurious hole covering" (MSHC) rule (Getz and Wilmers 2004). The T-LoCoH R package (Lyons, Turner and Getz 2013) recommends choosing the parameter empirically by examining how isopleth area and spurious holes change across a range of values.
When you specify a length, it may be entered in any linear unit and is converted to meters internally; the adaptive cumulative distance is reported in the unit you chose. Screen out obvious location errors before running, as LoCoH is sensitive to outliers.
References: • Getz and Wilmers (2004) Ecography 27:489-505, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0906-7590.2004.03835.x • Getz et al. (2007) PLoS ONE 2(2):e207, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000207 • Lyons, Turner and Getz (2013) Movement Ecology 1:2, https://doi.org/10.1186/2051-3933-1-2
Environments: this tool honors the Output Coordinate System environment. If it is set to a coordinate system other than the input's, the output polygons are reprojected to it as a last step; areas, point counts, densities, and the adaptive distance remain computed in the input coordinate system. No other geoprocessing environments affect this tool.

dialogReference.para: The point features (for example, GPS or VHF telemetry fixes) from which the local hulls are built. May be in a geographic or projected coordinate system; empty or null geometries are ignored.

param.name: a_method
param.expression: Maximum distance between any pair of points | Specify a length

dialogReference.para: How the maximum cumulative length a is determined. Maximum distance between any pair of points sets a automatically (the Getz et al. 2007 heuristic). Specify a length enables the Length parameter so you can enter a value.

The maximum cumulative length a, used only when Specify a length is chosen. Enter a value in any linear unit; it is converted to meters for the computation, and the adaptive cumulative distance is reported in the unit you choose.

Output polygon feature class of the dissolved cumulative LoCoH isopleths. Each feature stores its dissolved area (Area), enclosed point count (Point_Count), point proportion (Point_Proportion), and the adaptive cumulative distance (Adaptive_Cumulative_Dist).
Optional output polygon feature class of the individual local convex hulls, each with its own area and the cumulative count, proportion, and adaptive distance at its rank.

scriptExample.title: LoCoH (Adaptive) example
scriptExample.para: Run an adaptive LoCoH using the maximum distance between any pair of points, creating the cumulative isopleths and the individual hulls.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your installed path is shown in this tool's run messages arcpy.jenness.LoCoHAdaptive( "Owl_6_Points", "Maximum distance between any pair of points", None, r"C:\Project\HomeRanges.gdb\Owl_6_Points_Adaptive_Cumulative", r"C:\Project\HomeRanges.gdb\Owl_6_Points_Adaptive_Hulls")

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Adaptive (a-) Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) home-range and utilization-distribution estimator (Getz et al. 2007).
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Estimates an animal's home range and utilization distribution using the Adaptive (a-) Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) method of Getz et al. (2007). For every input point, the tool sorts the other points by distance and adds them (nearest first) until their cumulative distance reaches the maximum cumulative length a; the convex hull of the focal point and its selected neighbours becomes its local hull. Hulls are sorted by point count and merged cumulatively into density isopleths, each attributed with its dissolved area, enclosed point count and proportion, and the adaptive cumulative distance. The value of a can be set automatically to the maximum distance between any pair of points (the Getz et al. 2007 heuristic) or specified as a length in any linear unit, which is converted to meters for the computation. Distances use the Haversine formula for geographic data and planar distance converted to meters for projected data. The primary output is the dissolved cumulative isopleths; an optional second output contains the individual hulls. Method reference: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000207
